artifacts.summary: Audits the redeploy-remedy delivery gap: found 13 remedy-string emission sites across 9 scripts (task description named only 3), corrected a test-attribution error (test-deploy-freshness.sh actually covers check-deploy-freshness.sh, not verify-deploy.sh), confirmed both test suites only substring-match on "deploy-headless.sh" (safe to enrich), and recorded rulings on Half A delivery form, Half B presentation, and all three ALSO RULE ON questions.

memory_candidates.content: When grepping a source store for 'every X emission site' style task scopes, re-grep broadly (combine the mechanism name with likely surrounding verbs like Remedy/regenerate/redeploy) rather than trusting a task description's named list -- in one audit the real count was ~13 sites across 9 files against a task description naming only 3, and the task's own GOAL/ACCEPTANCE phrasing ('every ... emission site') already implied the wider scope was intended.

Before editing a pattern doc's 'generated-copy source' canonical bullet block (e.g. bounded-build-waiter.md's 'Copy this exact text' section, propagated by lint to N agent files), check whether the needed addition can instead live in ordinary surrounding prose -- editing the canonical block itself forces a full re-propagation pass and risks failing the lint check (e.g. lint-agent-contracts.sh Check H), while prose elsewhere in the same file carries no such obligation.

A test asserting assert_contains/== *substring* on a diagnostic/remedy string only checks the literal substring, not exact wording -- this gives wide latitude to enrich such strings (e.g. adding a required-step instruction) without any test update, as long as the asserted substring is preserved. Always read the actual assertion line rather than assuming an exact-match test exists.
